content.text: medically managed pts: osteoporosis is treated w bisphosphonates; for marked hypercalcemia: calcitonin (salmon) 4 to 8 IU/kg SC every 12 h; can ↓Ca by 1 to 2 mg/dL within a few hours.

Tx of osteoporosis in postmenopausal women and in men: 10 mg daily or 70 mg (tablet or oral solution) once weekly. Swallow tablets whole w/ 6-8 ounces plain water at least 30 min b4 the first food, drink, or medication of the day. ⍉ lie down for at least 30 min after taking and until after food.

CI: abnormalities of the esophagus which delay esophageal emptying such as stricture or achalasia. CI: inability to stand or sit upright for at least 30 min. CI: hypocalcemia. Esophageal reactions (esophagitis, ulcers, erosions) reported; be alert for signs and instruct pts to discontinue and seek medical attention for dysphagia, odynophagia, retrosternal pain, or new/worsening heartburn. Hypocalcemia must be corrected b4 initiating therapy. Severe bone, joint, muscle pain may occur; discontinue use if severe symptoms develop. ONJ reported (can occur spontaneously; generally associated w/ tooth extraction and/or local infection w/ delayed healing). Atypical fractures incl femoral fractures reported; pts w/ new thigh or groin pain should be evaluated to rule out a femoral fracture; re-evaluate risk/benefit and consider interrupting bisphosphonate therapy. Not recommended if CrCl less than 35 mL/min. Calcium, antacids, or oral medications containing multivalent cations interfere w/ absorption; instruct pts to wait at least one-half hour after FOSAMAX b4 any other oral medication. OD: hypocalcemia, hypophosphatemia, and upper GI adverse events may result; give milk or antacids to bind alendronate; ⍉ induce vomiting (risk of esophageal irritation); keep the pt fully upright.

CI: hypersensitivity to calcitonin salmon or any of the excipients (reactions incl anaphylaxis w/ death, bronchospasm, and swelling of the tongue or throat). Serious hypersensitivity reactions incl fatal anaphylaxis reported; consider skin testing b4 treatment in pts w/ suspected hypersensitivity to calcitonin salmon. Hypocalcemia w/ tetany (muscle cramps, twitching) and seizure activity reported; hypocalcemia must be corrected b4 initiating therapy. Meta-analysis of 21 trials suggests an ↑ risk of overall malignancies in calcitonin salmon-treated pts. Circulating antibodies to calcitonin salmon may develop and may cause loss of response to treatment. Use for Paget's dz or postmenopausal osteoporosis is recommended w/ an adequate intake of Ca and vitamin D. Concomitant lithium may ↓ plasma lithium concentrations (↑ urinary clearance); lithium dose may require adjustment. OD: hypocalcemic tetany could occur; keep parenteral calcium available for treatment. Most common adverse reactions: nausea w/ or w/o vomiting (10%), injection site inflammation (10%), and flushing of the face or hands (2% to 5%). Due to the possible association between malignancy and calcitonin salmon use, the need for continued therapy should be re-evaluated periodically.
